app.name: AgroShift UZ
app.description: Helps farmers in Uzbekistan compare crop rotations for their own field using NASA Earth observations, local soil information, crop characteristics and their own priorities.
nav.label: Main navigation
lang.label: Language
common.disclaimer: This tool supports, not replaces, your judgment and your agronomist's advice.
landing.title: Compare crop rotations for your field
landing.lead: AgroShift UZ uses NASA Earth observations, local soil information, crop characteristics and your own priorities to compare rotations for farms in Uzbekistan.
landing.pitch_data: For each demo farm it shows 20 years of climate, what the satellite saw on the field and the soil, then ranks rotations by what matters to you: water, soil health, feed, market, risk.
landing.pitch_judgment: Every number has a source and a confidence level, and the tool says where your own judgment and your agronomist's advice matter most.
field.title: Your field
about.title: About AgroShift UZ
about.lead: AgroShift UZ helps farmers and advisers in Uzbekistan compare crop rotations for one field. It combines NASA Earth observations with soil data, crop characteristics and the farmer's own priorities, and shows every number with its source and a confidence level.
about.sources.title: Data sources
about.sources.lead: NASA datasets are marked. Citations are quoted as the providers ask.
about.use.power: Daily maximum and minimum temperature and rain since 2006 for ~50 km cells (MERRA-2 reanalysis; GEOS-IT for the latest months): climate calendar, frost dates, heat days, evaporative demand, trends and the stress test.
about.use.mod13q1: Vegetation greenness (NDVI) every 16 days at 250 m: what the satellite saw on the field, bare periods and the check against the farmer's answer.
about.use.mcd12q1: Land cover: only cropland pixels (classes 12 and 14) are used for the field's greenness curve.
about.use.ornl: The web service through which the MODIS data above are fetched for small windows around each field.
about.use.soilgrids: Topsoil (0–30 cm) pH, organic carbon, clay, sand and silt — modelled values that a soil test replaces.
about.use.dem: Elevation of the field and four neighbours 100 m away, for the slope.
about.use.geoboundaries: Borders of Uzbekistan and its 14 regions.
about.versions_unavailable: Data versions are not available right now.
about.methods.title: Methods
about.methods.lead: All calculations are open source (src/lib/ in the code repository) and covered by unit tests.
about.method.climate: Climate statistics use the complete years {from}–{to} of daily data; a year with more than {missing} % missing days is left out.
about.method.et0: Evaporative demand (ET0): the Hargreaves equation (FAO-56, eq. 52) with extraterrestrial radiation from latitude and date (FAO-56, eq. 21–25).
about.method.rain: Effective rain: the monthly formula of Brouwer & Heibloem (1986).
about.method.water: Irrigation water: crop coefficient by growth stage (FAO-56 Kc curve) × ET0, minus effective rain, divided by the irrigation efficiency (furrow {furrow} %, sprinkler {sprinkler} %, drip {drip} %). The dry-year value is the {percentile}th percentile over the years.
about.method.frost: Frost dates: last spring and first autumn day with a minimum temperature of 0 °C or less; the dates "safe in 80 % of years" are percentiles over the years.
about.method.trends: Trends: Sen's slope with the Mann–Kendall test; a change is called a trend only when p < {alpha}.
about.method.ndvi: Satellite greenness: median NDVI of the reliable cropland pixels in a 1 km window; the field counts as bare below {bare} and green from {green}.
about.method.satellite: Satellite check: the last {years} complete years are compared with the expected crop cover of the farmer's rotation; differences lasting at least {runs} composites (48 days) are reported.
about.method.fit: Crop fit: trapezoid scores for temperature and pH (EcoCrop style), salinity yield loss after Maas & Hoffman (FAO-29) and season length against the frost dates; the lowest score limits the crop ({good} and more: recommended, {risky}–{risky_top}: risky, below {risky}: not suitable).
about.method.rotation: Rotations: a typical-year calendar from the median sowing and harvest dates, then bare-soil days, erosion exposure, legume seasons, organic matter, runs of one plant family, frost and harvest-rain risk, salinity loss and forage value.
about.method.ranking: Ranking: each metric is scaled from 0 to 1 on fixed, documented ranges (never relative to the other options) and weighted by the farmer's priorities; an unreliable water supply raises the water weight.
about.method.scenario: Stress test (delta-change method): the temperature change is added to every daily value and daily rain is scaled, then the whole calculation is run again. It is a what-if test, not a forecast.
about.assumptions.title: Assumptions
about.assumption.crops: Crop parameters (data/crops.json) were compiled from FAO tables and local practice with AI assistance. Values not yet reviewed by an agronomist are marked "estimated" in the app.
about.assumption.cotton: Cotton is sown once the 7-day mean temperature passes 16 °C, but not before 15 April (local practice).
about.assumption.ph: Cotton, winter wheat, winter barley, sorghum, alfalfa and mung bean tolerate calcareous soils: pH optimum up to 8.2, absolute limit 8.8–9.0.
about.assumption.heat: Heat days come from regional air temperature (~50 km), which is warmer than an irrigated field, so heat is a low-confidence warning and never excludes a crop.
about.assumption.efficiency: Irrigation efficiencies, NDVI thresholds and class breaks of the map layers are documented assumptions, not measurements for a field.
about.assumption.dry_year: The "Dry year" preset reduces rain by 30 % on every day; the dry-year (90th percentile) irrigation need is shown separately in every scenario.
about.assumption.defaults: Each demo farm starts from a common rotation chosen by the team (Karakalpakstan: cotton every year, as the satellite shows; the others: cotton–wheat); a map point starts from cotton–wheat; every priority starts at 1. The farmer changes all of these in step 3.
about.assumption.decisions: Every decision of this kind is listed in DECISIONS.md in the code repository.
about.limits.title: Limitations
about.limit.power: NASA POWER is a reanalysis for ~50 km cells: it describes the regional climate, not your field.
about.limit.modis: One 250 m MODIS pixel can mix several fields, trees and roads; the app says when few pixels are cropland.
about.limit.soil: SoilGrids values are modelled, not measured; a soil test from your field always replaces them.
about.limit.salinity: There is no public field-level salinity map of Uzbekistan. Salinity is shown as unknown unless you enter a soil test or the team adds a sourced regional table.
about.limit.money: No prices, costs or incomes are computed, and the water for salt leaching, canal losses and groundwater use is not included.
about.limit.advice: Results are for comparison and discussion with your agronomist, not instructions.
about.glossary.title: Glossary
about.ai.title: Use of AI
about.ai.code: The code and most texts of this app were written with Claude, an AI assistant made by Anthropic (through Claude Code), directed and reviewed by the team.
about.ai.data: The draft crop parameters were compiled with AI assistance and are marked as estimated until an agronomist reviews them. All other numbers come from the cited data and the documented formulas, never from an AI model.
about.ai.translations: The Uzbek and Russian texts were drafted with AI assistance and are being proofread by native speakers on the team.

rotation.why.cotton_mono: Cotton every year: the common baseline under cotton cluster contracts, shown so the other options can be compared with it.
rotation.why.cotton_wheat: The standard cotton–wheat system. After the wheat harvest in June the field usually stays bare until cotton is sown the next spring.
rotation.why.cotton_wheat_mung: Cotton–wheat with a mung bean second crop (takroriy ekin) sown after the wheat harvest, so the field is covered in summer and a legume adds nitrogen.
rotation.why.alfalfa_cotton_wheat: The traditional soil-restoring rotation: three years of alfalfa add organic matter and nitrogen before cotton returns.
rotation.why.barley_sorghum: Suggested for saline or water-short fields: winter barley grows on winter and spring moisture, and sorghum is drought-tolerant and moderately salt-tolerant.
rotation.why.wheat_silage: For forage and livestock farms: silage maize sown after the wheat harvest gives a second feed harvest in the same year.
rotation.why.rainfed_wheat_chickpea: For rain-fed (lalmi) land: chickpea breaks the cereal cycle and, as a legume, adds nitrogen.

stress.title: Stress test: what if the weather were different?
stress.lead: The whole calculation is re-run on the daily weather observed {from}–{to}, changed as set below: sowing and frost dates, crop stress, water need, feasibility and ranking.
stress.applied: Calculated for {dt} °C and {rain} % rain on every day of the record.

stress.confidence_note: Confidence is unchanged by the scenario: it describes the data, not the weather.
stress.climate_spring: Last spring frost (80 % of years before)
stress.climate_autumn: First autumn frost (80 % of years after)
glossary.ndvi: NDVI (Normalised Difference Vegetation Index) measures how green the land is from space: about 0.1 for bare soil, 0.3–0.5 for a young crop and 0.6–0.9 for a dense green crop.
glossary.salinity: Salinity is measured as the electrical conductivity of a saturated soil paste (ECe, dS/m). Above about 4 dS/m many crops lose yield; cotton and barley tolerate more than beans or maize.
glossary.et: The water a well-watered reference grass would lose to the air through evaporation and plant transpiration in a day, in mm. It measures how "thirsty" the weather is; crops need about this much times their crop coefficient.
glossary.soil_moisture: How much wetter or drier the root zone is than usual for that month. NASA POWER models it without irrigation, so on irrigated land it shows the weather, not the field.
glossary.reanalysis: A best estimate of past weather made by combining many observations with a weather model, on a regular grid (here about 50 km). Consistent over time, but not a measurement on your field.
glossary.frost_free: The days between the last spring frost and the first autumn frost: the time a frost-sensitive crop such as cotton has to grow.
glossary.rotation: The order of crops grown on the same field over the years, such as cotton one year and wheat the next. Changing crops breaks pest cycles and can rebuild the soil.
glossary.double_cropping: Two harvests from one field in one year, such as mung bean or maize sown right after the wheat harvest in June (takroriy ekin).
